seoTitle: Custom Logo Perfume: Private Label Guide | TopPerfume
description: Plan a custom logo perfume order: compare branding options, prepare your artwork, confirm MOQ and samples, and send a clear brief for a private label quote.
excerpt: Learn what to confirm before adding your logo to a fragrance product, from eligible packaging and artwork to quantity, sampling and a written quotation.
title: Custom Logo Perfume: A Private Label Buying Guide
html:
A perfume with your logo starts with a few practical decisions: which product you want to sell, where your branding should appear, and what needs to be approved before production. Getting those decisions clear makes the first quotation more useful—and gives you a better basis for comparing options.

This guide is for retailers and new beauty brands planning a fragrance project. It explains how to prepare a brief, separate different types of customization, and move from an idea to a sample and quotation.

Choose the buying route that matches your plan

Begin by deciding whether you want to purchase finished products for resale or develop a product under your own brand. The available products, minimum quantities and approval steps can differ.

Buying route What you are asking for What to confirm first
Finished-product wholesale An existing product for your retail assortment Exact product reference, quantity, packaging and current availability
Your logo on an eligible product Your brand identity applied through an agreed branding route Product eligibility, logo position, available method and minimum quantity
A wider development project Changes to packaging, fragrance direction or other product details Feasible scope, samples, separate costs and project timing

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner, reviewing custom projects with suppliers individually. Our low-MOQ perfume and private-label page sets out the current routes. Its starting quantities apply to eligible options; the final scope is confirmed against your brief.

If you are browsing finished products carrying an existing brand, ask us to identify an appropriate private-label option for your project. Buying a branded wholesale product and commissioning your own branded product are separate requests.

Decide where your logo should appear

Think about how a customer will see and handle the product. The bottle is one part of the presentation; the carton, label and other agreed packaging elements may also carry your brand information.

Prepare a simple placement list. For each part, identify what you want to show: the brand name, product name, design element or other approved text. Ask which branding methods are available for the selected component before fixing the artwork.

Questions worth resolving early include:

  • Is the proposed logo position suitable for this bottle or packaging surface?
  • What usable area and artwork dimensions should the designer work to?
  • Which colours and finishes are available for this specific option?
  • Will the quotation cover the bottle branding, outer box or both?
  • What additional product information must be accommodated in the final artwork for the intended market?

Treat a reference image as a way to explain your preferred direction. The agreed specification and approved sample should identify what will actually be supplied.

Prepare the product brief before polishing the design

A useful first message describes the business and product decisions as well as the logo. You can begin while some choices are still open: mark them as questions so the quotation addresses them directly.

Brief field What to include
Business and customers Your shop or brand, target customers and sales channel
Product direction Perfume, fragrance mist or another requested format; preferred size
Fragrance direction Your description of the scent you want to explore, if relevant
Branding scope Bottle, label, carton or other requested elements
Quantity Estimated units, with a breakdown by product or version
Artwork status Logo available, artwork in progress, or guidance requested
Destination Country and city for the shipping discussion
Timing Your preferred launch date and any fixed deadline
Budget A purchasing budget or target cost, if you have one

For example, “one fragrance product with our logo on the bottle and carton” is a clearer starting scope than “fully custom perfume.” It allows the supplier to explain what is available and which decisions still affect the quotation.

Confirm how the minimum quantity is counted

Ask whether the minimum applies per fragrance, bottle size, packaging version or artwork design. A quantity spread across several versions may be treated differently from the same quantity of one confirmed item.

TopPerfume’s current route page lists selected logo and private-label options from 100 pieces. This is a starting point for eligible projects. Ask for the minimum quantity and available configuration for the exact product you are discussing.

Also ask what changes if you revise the bottle, fragrance, decoration or outer packaging. A finished-product wholesale minimum should not be used to budget a different custom project.

Review artwork and samples in separate steps

An artwork layout helps you review placement and text. A physical sample allows you to inspect the supplied materials and appearance. Ask which type of sample is available at each stage and what it represents.

Before approving the project, review:

  • The correct brand spelling, product wording and agreed artwork version.
  • Logo size, position and appearance on the selected component.
  • The bottle, cap and packaging configuration included in the quotation.
  • The selected fragrance sample or product reference, where applicable.
  • Any differences between the sample and the proposed bulk order.

Keep the approval record specific. Use a dated reference and an agreed list of components, rather than relying on a general “looks good” message. Ask for sample charges and shipping costs to be stated before proceeding.

Request a quotation with an agreed scope

Your quotation should identify the product, quantity, branding work and packaging included. Ask whether there are separate artwork, setup, sample or shipping charges, and which costs remain to be confirmed.

Discuss the timeline as stages: specification confirmation, artwork approval, sample review and dispatch planning. The applicable timing depends on the selected project. A general website dispatch indication should not become a fixed arrival promise for an unconfirmed custom order.

For repeat orders, ask how the approved specification will be referenced and whether availability, quantity requirements or pricing need to be reconfirmed.

Questions buyers often ask

Can I start by adding a logo without developing a new fragrance?

Ask about the existing options eligible for your own branding. Your logo brief can be reviewed separately from a new fragrance-development request; availability is confirmed by product and supplier.

Do I need finished artwork before contacting you?

You can start with a product direction, estimated quantity and preferred logo position. State whether your logo is ready and request the applicable artwork requirements before preparing the final layout.

Can I split the order across several designs?

Include the proposed quantity for each version in your brief. The minimum and setup arrangements must be checked for that configuration.

Does a catalogue product automatically support my own logo?

Customization eligibility is reviewed separately. Identify the product or format you like and ask which private-label options are suitable.

Discuss your custom logo perfume project

Send your product direction, logo placement, estimated quantity and destination through the TopPerfume contact page. If some details are undecided, include those questions in the brief.

You can also compare the existing wholesale and private-label routes before requesting a quotation. The aim of the first conversation is to identify a suitable product and a clear scope for the next decision.

description: Plan your first wholesale perfume order with a clear customer profile, sample shortlist, SKU quantities, cost comparison and supplier questions before you buy.
excerpt: Build a focused first fragrance order by matching products to your customers, comparing samples and confirming product-by-product buying terms.
title: Buying Wholesale Perfume for a New Store: Your First-Order Guide
html:
Your first perfume order shapes what customers see, what your team can explain and how much money is committed to stock. Before adding more products, give each item a clear reason to be in the assortment.

This guide helps new fragrance shops, beauty retailers and online sellers prepare a focused wholesale order. Start with your customers, build a shortlist, compare samples and confirm the terms for each product before committing to quantities.

Describe the customer you want to serve

Write a short buying brief for your store. Include who you expect to buy, how they will discover the products and the type of purchase you want to support.

For example, are you planning a gift-focused display, adding fragrance to an existing beauty shop or opening an online assortment with a few clearly differentiated choices? These are planning directions, rather than predictions of what will sell.

Record four starting points:

  • Your customers and sales channel.
  • The intended retail price range.
  • Product formats and sizes you want to consider.
  • The amount you can allocate to stock, samples and delivery.

When you discuss options with a supplier, this brief helps explain why one product may fit your plan better than another.

Give each shortlisted product a role

You can build a small assortment around distinct customer preferences or shopping occasions. Ask for the product information and samples needed to evaluate each choice.

A planning sheet might look like this:

Role in the assortment Candidate product Question to resolve before buying Planned quantity
An everyday fragrance option Add a product link Does the sample fit the customer preference you are targeting? Decide after review
A different scent direction Add a product link Is the difference clear enough to explain to a customer? Decide after review
A gift-focused option Add a product link Are the presentation, size and total cost suitable? Decide after review
A possible later addition Keep a reference What evidence would justify adding this product? Leave out of the first order if undecided

The rows are a planning example, not a fixed bundle or a recommendation to stock four specific products. Use only the roles that make sense for your business.

Browse the TopPerfume fragrance collection to identify actual product references. Where fragrance notes or other details are not listed, ask for the information rather than inferring it from the bottle colour or product name.

Compare samples before deciding the full quantity

For each sample, record the product name, size and the reference supplied. Keep scent preference separate from packaging observations so you can explain why you prefer one option.

You may want to compare:

  • Your impression of the fragrance and how it develops during your observation.
  • How you would describe it to your intended customers.
  • The spray, cap, bottle and packaging as received.
  • Whether the supplied product information answers your retail questions.

Use reasonably consistent conditions when comparing samples, and record the time and context of any longevity observations. Your own sample notes support a buying decision; they are not a substitute for substantiated product performance claims.

Ask the supplier to clarify any mismatch between the sample, the product description and the proposed bulk supply before proceeding.

Confirm buying terms product by product

A low minimum advertised for one item does not establish the minimum for an entire catalogue. Check the exact SKU and any variants you want to order.

For example, the Lattafa Khamrah 100 mL product page provides an individual product reference and its listed order terms. Use the current page and a written quotation for that item, then repeat the check for each additional product.

Ask these questions:

  1. What is the current minimum for this exact product or variant?
  2. Can my proposed order contain different products, and what minimum applies to each?
  3. Is the requested quantity available for the planned order?
  4. What packaging is included with the quoted item?
  5. What sample, dispatch and delivery arrangements apply?

If your plan includes your own logo, describe it as a separate project. TopPerfume’s wholesale and private-label routes have different starting points and require product-specific confirmation.

Compare the cost of getting the order to your business

Keep the product subtotal separate from the full purchasing cost. Use the actual quotation for your destination and scope.

Cost item What to record
Products Unit price multiplied by the agreed quantity for each item
Samples Any agreed sample and sample-shipping charges
Extra work Agreed branding, packaging or other project charges, if applicable
Freight and handling The quoted transport scope and any stated exclusions
Other applicable charges Amounts confirmed for your transaction and destination

Compare suppliers on the same product specification, quantities and included services. If an amount is unknown, keep it visible as an item to confirm rather than treating it as zero.

TopPerfume’s order information explains that listed product subtotals exclude shipping and taxes and that transaction arrangements are agreed for each order.

Plan how you will explain the products

A useful assortment gives you clear information to share with shoppers. Prepare a short product card for each selected item using confirmed details.

Include the name, size, product presentation and any verified fragrance information. Add your own sample observations where appropriate, clearly identified as observations. If a customer asks about a detail you have not confirmed, return to the supplier for the information.

For online selling, use product images that match what you will supply. For a physical display, consider how the packaging and product information will help customers compare the choices. This preparation also reveals gaps before you purchase the full assortment.

Keep a simple first-order and reorder record

After launch, track what customers ask about, what sells and what remains in stock. Separate sales from interest: a product receiving questions may still need better information, a different presentation or further sample review.

Before placing the first order, ask how to identify the same product for a repeat purchase, how availability is confirmed and what buying terms may change. Keep the supplier reference and agreed specification with your order record.

Use your early results to decide whether to reorder, adjust quantities or add another product. A new item should have a clear role in the assortment.

Questions new buyers often ask

How many perfume products should a new store start with?

There is no fixed count in this guide. Choose a number you can sample, explain and fund within your plan. The planning sheet helps you give each selected product a purpose.

Can I mix different perfumes in one order?

Send the proposed product list and quantity for each item. Mixed-order eligibility and minimum quantities need to be confirmed against those products.

Should I begin with wholesale products or my own brand?

Decide what your first launch requires. Finished-product wholesale and a private-label project involve different product choices, quantities and approvals. Compare the actual options against your customers, budget and timing.

What information should I send to get a useful quote?

Include your destination, product links, quantity per item, planned timing and any sample or customization request. Mention the questions you still need help resolving.

Prepare your first wholesale perfume enquiry

Choose your candidates from the fragrance collection, then contact TopPerfume with your first-order brief.

Information Your first-order brief
Store type and customers Describe your business and intended buyers
Destination Country and city
Product references Paste the selected product links
Quantities List units for each product or variant
Samples State what you want to review first
Branding Standard wholesale or a separate logo/custom project
Timing and open questions Add your preferred schedule and what needs clarification

TopPerfume supports wholesale beauty sourcing and supplier coordination. Sharing a focused brief makes it easier to review product options, confirm the applicable terms and prepare the next step for your order.
